headline: Foundational skills and AI skills are not a trade-off.
standfirst: TRIAD studies how secondary schools can build AI competences without giving up foundational competences, inclusion or wellbeing. Eleven partners across seven countries are running the work, coordinated by RPTU Kaiserslautern.
newsletter_text: We send one email per project milestone, no more than four a year. Ask us to add you to the list.
newsletter_consent: I agree that TRIAD may store my email address to send the project newsletter. You can unsubscribe at any time.
framework_title: Three areas of competence, one framework
framework_text: TRIAD co-creates and tests an integrated framework that balances three areas of competence, with safeguards for learner wellbeing built in.

areas.title: AI and digital literacies
areas.detail: Using AI and digital tools with understanding

classroom_title: In classrooms, with learners aged 12 to 18
classroom_text: The project focuses on learners aged 12 to 18 in secondary schools and vocational education and training, where competences must be consolidated and inequality risks peak. Classroom scenarios are designed with teachers, school leaders and students, then tested in pilots across Europe.
find: When AI genuinely enhances learning rather than replacing it.
figure_caption: Three areas of competence held in balance, with learner wellbeing at the centre.
learners_text: One dot per learner. The EU-wide classroom pilots compare classes that use the AI-enriched scenarios with classes that do not, before and after, in Lithuania, Germany, Croatia, Finland, Italy and Greece.
